message.reasoning:
The user says: "start Docker on window using docker start." They want to start Docker on Windows using docker start. But docker start is used to start containers, not the Docker daemon. To start Docker service, you need to start the Docker Desktop or Docker Engine service. On Windows, you can use `net start com.docker.service` or `Start-Service -Name com.docker.service` in PowerShell. Or use Docker Desktop UI. The user might want to start Docker engine via command line. We can provide instructions: open PowerShell as admin and run `Start-Service -Name com.docker.service`. Or use `sc start com.docker.service`. Or if using Docker Desktop, you can start it via `& "$env:ProgramFiles\Docker\Docker\Docker Desktop.exe"`. But the user specifically says "using docker start". That is wrong. So we should explain that docker start starts containers, not the Docker daemon. To start Docker service, use `Start-Service` or `sc start`. Provide steps.

We can also mention that if Docker Desktop is installed, you can start it by launching the application. If you want to start the Docker daemon from command line, you can use `Start-Service com.docker.service`.

We can also mention that if you have Docker installed via Docker Desktop, you can use `docker-machine start default` if using Docker Machine. But likely they want to start Docker Desktop.

Thus answer: Use PowerShell: `Start-Service -Name com.docker.service`. Or `sc start com.docker.service`. Or use `docker-machine start default`. Also note that `docker start` is for containers.

We can also provide a script to start Docker Desktop: `& "$env:ProgramFiles\Docker\Docker\Docker Desktop.exe"`.
